titulo: The Tunguska Explosion: What Blew Up Over Siberia? #shorts
premisa: Told as a cold-case investigation. Act 1, the witness: June 30, 1908, about 7:15 a.m. You are Semyon Semenov, sitting on the porch of the Vanavara trading post in Siberia. The sky splits, a heat hits you like your shirt is on fire, and the shockwave throws you off your chair. You are about 40 miles from the center. Act 2, the impossible evidence: 830 square miles of forest are knocked flat, about 80 million trees, all pointing outward like matchsticks. That night the sky over Europe glows so bright people in London read the newspaper at midnight. Yet nobody goes there for 19 years. Act 3, the detective: in 1927 Leonid Kulik leads an expedition to find the giant meteorite. Clue 1: no crater. Clue 2: no space rock, not even a fragment worth digging up. Clue 3, the key one: at dead center the trees are still standing, upright but stripped bare, like telegraph poles. Reveal: that only makes sense if the blast came from straight above. A space rock about the size of a 15-story building exploded in mid-air, roughly 3 to 6 miles up. The shockwave hit the trees at the center from above and left them standing, while it knocked down everything around them. There was nothing left to hit the ground, so there was no crater.
gancho: What blew up over Siberia with the power of 1,000 Hiroshimas… and left no crater? Nobody ever found what hit.
